title: Grateful Dead Live at Henry J. Kaiser Convention Center on 1985-09-12
source: Matrix 3 Source Mix - SBD (shn id 11803) Master Soundboard Cassette > DAT > CDR; via StoryTeller; Seeded to etree by steve barbella + AUD (shn id 118324)  flac24; Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Darby; SennheiserMD421's (PAS/DFC Row 2 Balcony/3.5 Feet High)> Sony TC-D5M,Tapes Maxell MX; Transfer Information:Tascam 112 MKII (XLR Out)>Tascam HD-P2 @ 24/48> HDD>Amadeus Pro (tracking/Fades/FLAC8); Tracks Renamed/Metadata Tagging With AudioGate Software By Keo + VID (noshnid) VIDEO Patches supplied by audio from a video sent by Russ C. and worked on by BHP - matrix mixing by Kevin Tobin

ai_review.summary: Matrix source gives a clearer, more continuous sound despite a glitchy board, and while Garcia’s vocals are weak, the jam-heavy performance keeps it enjoyable.
ai_review.review: The recording benefits from a matrix mix that smooths out board glitches and adds ambience, though the high‑frequency range can be a bit harsh. Musically the show suffers from Garcia’s “vocal aphasia,” but strong improvisational jams compensate enough to lift the overall impression.

ai_rating.rationale: Limited review data (only two comments) with mixed opinions; show quality is average and recording is decent, yielding a modest combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Board is described as glitchy and slightly sterile; matrix mix adds continuity and distances vocals (preferred). Some EQ adjustment suggested to tame 4‑16 kHz highs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Garcia’s vocal issues are noted, but the set is rescued by tasty jams and a strong improvisational vibe throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as weak/aphasic, yet his jam space is praised for being tasty and engaging.
